cards.text: Hosea is a prophet, and this is a message from the LORD about His people, Israel. The LORD starts way back, when Israel was a child, and He says He loved him. Friend, this is a dad pulling out the OLD baby pictures.

cards.question: When Israel was a child, the LORD loved him and called His son out of ___.

cards.text: So the LORD keeps calling Israel, over and over. Let's see how that goes.

cards.question: The more the LORD called Israel, the closer they came to Him.
While Israel kept walking away from the LORD, who were they sacrificing to?

cards.text: Now the LORD gets tender: He calls Israel Ephraim here too, and He says He taught Ephraim to walk, holding them by the arms. I've watched toddlers walk, friend, and it's mostly falling forward with confidence.

cards.question: Ephraim realized it was the LORD who healed them.
The LORD taught Ephraim to walk. How does He say He led them?

cards.text: Cords of kindness, ropes of love. Then He lifted the yoke off their necks, like that heavy bag strap finally sliding off your shoulder at the end of a LONG day.

cards.question: After lifting the yoke from their necks, the LORD bent down to ___ them.

cards.text: Then the message turns, and the LORD asks: won't they go back to Egypt and be ruled by the nation of Assyria? Egypt, friend, the place He called them OUT of.

cards.question: Why does the LORD say Israel is headed back to Egypt and under Assyria?

cards.text: A sword will flash through their cities and destroy the bars of their gates. They get consumed in their own plans, like a to-do list that ends up running YOU.
And the LORD says His people are bent on turning from Him. Not wandering off by accident, BENT on it.

cards.question: Even though Israel calls to the Most High, He will by no means lift them up.

cards.text: Right about now you'd expect the hammer to come down. Instead, the LORD stops and asks Ephraim a question.

cards.question: Right after all those warnings, what does the LORD ask Ephraim?

answers.text: How could I give you up

cards.text: He keeps asking. How could He make them like Admah, or treat them like Zeboiim? Those are towns the LORD overthrew along with Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:23).

cards.question: The LORD says His heart is turned within Him and His ___ is stirred.

cards.text: Then the LORD stops asking and starts answering. Lean in for this one, friend.

cards.question: The LORD says He will execute the full fury of His anger on Ephraim.
Why does the LORD say He won't destroy Ephraim again?

answers.text: He is God and not man
The prophet begged Him to stop

cards.question: The LORD, the Holy One among His people, says He will come in wrath.

cards.text: Then the LORD looks ahead: His people will walk after the LORD. He's also going to make a sound nobody could sleep through, not even the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: Looking ahead, the LORD says He will roar like a ___.
When the LORD roars, His children run away from Him.

cards.text: They come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. DOVES, friend, and my Minty would be passing notes down the whole counter about this one.

cards.question: After His children come trembling back, where does the LORD settle them?

answers.text: In a city by the sea

cards.text: And the LORD signs it Himself: declares the LORD. I know what it's like to get called out of a dark place, friend, so hearing Him promise to settle His children in their homes gets me every single time.

findings.problem: The card says Hosea is a prophet. That fact comes from outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Hosea 11:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Their king sold them out" uses a modern idiom. The right answer, "They refused to repent," sounds like the Bible. The difference in tone makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: In Hosea 11:6, the sword destroys the people through their own plans. A to-do list "running you" is about being bossed around by your tasks, not being destroyed by your own schemes. The comparison doesn't share the core action, and it lands as a light gag in the middle of a judgment of slaughter.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup "you'd expect the hammer to come down. Instead..." tells the baker the next line won't be harsh. That rules out the two harsh wrong answers on card 2 ("Why should I keep you" and "Who will save you now") and leaves only the right one.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "He keeps asking.", the Admah/Zeboiim question, and the Deuteronomy explanation. Only the opening card may go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Then the LORD stops asking and starts answering. Lean in for this one, friend." tells nothing from Hosea 11:9, yet the card cites that verse. It is only a transition.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card tells the baker that His people "will walk after the LORD." That gives away the answer to card 11, the true/false about whether His children run away from Him when He roars.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
